background_therapy.source_excerpt: Permitted Concomitant Therapy: Unless specified as prohibited therapies (see Section 9.10.3), all therapies are authorized, including basic skin care (cleansing and bathing), moisturizers, bleach baths, and topical anesthetics. Starting from the screening visit, subjects can use their daily moisturizer, if it does not contain any compound with known anti-itch effect... Subjects should not change emollients or moisturizers or apply products for itching relief during the course of the study. ... Prohibited Therapy: Treatment with the following concomitant medications/therapies in Table 4 is prohibited during the study unless otherwise specified. Table 4. Prohibited Therapy [lists topical calcineurin inhibitors/TCS, vitamin D analogs, PDE-4 inhibitors, systemic/intralesional corticosteroids, oral antihistamines, sedatives, phototherapy, immunosuppressants, biologics, dupilumab, systemic retinoids, gabapentinoids, cannabinoids, investigational drugs, alternative medicine, vaccines with specific washout timeframes].

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: To control the type I error at 5%, a fixed sequential testing approach will be implemented. For testing purposes, both primary endpoints will be tested first in a predefined order as listed in Section 5.1 at 5% significance level, and testing of key secondary endpoints will start only if both primary endpoints are successful at 5% level of significance. Key secondary endpoints will be tested in an order listed in Section 5.2, stopping when non-significant result (p > 0.05) is found. The primary endpoints include: the proportion of subjects with an improvement of >=4 from baseline in PP NRS at Week 16; the proportion of subjects reporting success on the IGA at Week 16...

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Duration: [...] weeks, including a screening period (up to 4 weeks), a 24-week treatment period, and an 8-week follow-up. ... At the end of the 24-week treatment period, consenting subjects may be eligible to enter an active treatment/long-term extension (LTE) study (RD.06.SPR.202699). Subjects who participate in the LTE are not required to complete the follow-up visit. Subjects who do not participate in the LTE will return for a follow-up visit at Week 32 (12 weeks after the last study drug [administration])... During the treatment period, eligible subjects will be randomized to receive either nemolizumab (CD14152) or placebo, administered Q4W for 24 weeks (last injection at Week 20).

value.rationale: If deemed to be medically necessary by the investigator (e.g. to control intolerable PN signs/symptoms), rescue therapies can be prescribed. Rescue therapy must not be prescribed during the screening period, and as a general guideline should not be prescribed within the first 4 weeks after baseline to allow a minimum time for study drug exposure.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: Rescue Therapy: If deemed to be medically necessary by the investigator (eg, to control intolerable PN signs/symptoms), rescue therapies can be prescribed to the subjects. Rescue therapy must not be prescribed during the screening period. As a general guideline and per individual investigator judgment, rescue therapy should not be prescribed within the first 4 weeks after baseline... Rescue therapies include: Topical corticosteroids, Topical calcineurin inhibitors, Oral antihistamines, Systemic or intralesional corticosteroids, Biologics (including their biosimilars), Systemic nonsteroidal immunosuppressants/immunomodulators, Phototherapy, Gabapentinoids. Whenever possible, investigators should first use topical medication or oral antihistamines as rescue therapy before escalating to other systemic therapies. If subjects receive topical treatments, oral antihistamines, or UVB phototherapy as rescue therapy, study drug administration should be continued... If subjects receive systemic rescue therapy (other than oral antihistamines), intralesional corticosteroids, or oral PUVA treatment, the study drug administration must be permanently discontinued... For the purpose of efficacy analysis, subjects receiving any rescue therapies will be considered as treatment failures.
